newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index peak to attract sellers-First Boston.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index peak to attract sellers-First Boston.

text.p: India's booming stock markets are likely to test its all-time highs in the short-run but face a tough task to stay at that level, an official of Credit Suisse First Boston said on Tuesday.
"Yes I think so because there is a lot of momentum now," K.R. Bharat, managing director at securities firm, C.S. First Boston told Reuters Financial Television in reply to a question.
He had been asked whether the Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) benchmark 30-share index will hit its all-time high. The record high of 4,643.31 was set on September 12, 1994.
"As I said there is a lot of liquidity in the system as well and we think for sure there will be a test of the all-time (closing) highs which is 4,630."

On Tuesday, the Bombay index rallied for a second straight day, adding 82.65 points, or 1.85 points to end at 4,548.02. The index hit a 34-month high on Monday, piercing the 4,450 level for the first time since mid-September 1994.
But, Bharat said he expected heavy selling to come up near the market's peak.

"Having said that, I think there will be considerable selling pressure at those levels because what we also need to understand is that when foreign investors were first allowed to invest in the Indian equity markets in 1993, the index was at these levels."
"And so, foreign investors haven't really made much money in the Indian markets until today. And I think there will be some selling pressure when the all-time high is reached."
Bharat said the stock markets had shown a sharp rise on the back of rising liquidity and anticipation of an economic turnaround in the Indian economy this year.
A currency crisis in South East Asian markets had also benefited Indian markets as the rupee enjoyed "relative currency stability," he said.
